slides.heading: 10 T-codes every ABAP developer *uses daily*
items: SE38 / SE80 - Write and browse programs
SE16N - Look at table data fast
ST05 - SQL trace for slow reports

posts.caption:
Save this list. You will use it every single day.

The 10 T-codes that cover most of an ABAP developer's work:
SE38/SE80 to write code, SE11 for the dictionary, SE16N to check data, ST22 to read dumps and ST05 to catch slow SQL.

Knowing these by heart makes you noticeably faster, and interviewers expect it.

Which T-code do you open first every morning? Tell us in the comments.

slides.title: Why is your *report so slow*
slides.voiceover: आपकी report slow है? वजह शायद ये है।
slides.spoken: Aapki report slow hai? Wajah shayad ye hai.

slides.heading: *Slow* vs *fast*
slides.left:
LOOP AT lt_orders INTO DATA(ls).
  SELECT SINGLE name1 FROM kna1
    WHERE kunnr = @ls-kunnr
    INTO @DATA(lv_name).
ENDLOOP.
slides.right:
SELECT kunnr, name1 FROM kna1
  FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @lt_orders
  WHERE kunnr = @lt_orders-kunnr
  INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_kna1).
slides.voiceover: Loop के अंदर SELECT, मतलब हर row पर database call. एक बार में पढ़ो, फिर memory से उठाओ।
slides.spoken: Loop ke andar SELECT, matlab har row par database call. Ek baar mein padho, phir memory se uthao.

slides.title: Result
slides.detail: Then read lt_kna1 inside the loop.
slides.voiceover: दस हज़ार calls की जगह, सिर्फ एक। Save कर लो।
slides.spoken: Das hazaar calls ki jagah, sirf ek. Save kar lo.

posts.caption:
Is your report taking 20 minutes instead of 2?

In most cases the cause is the same: a SELECT inside a LOOP. Every iteration is a separate trip to the database.

The fix: read the data once before the loop (JOIN or FOR ALL ENTRIES), then look it up in an internal table inside the loop. For large volumes, use a SORTED or HASHED table.

Save this for your next code review.

slides.title: A full *ALV report* in 5 lines
slides.voiceover: ALV report सिर्फ पाँच lines में? Field catalog की ज़रूरत ही नहीं।
slides.spoken: ALV report sirf paanch lines mein? Field catalog ki zaroorat hi nahi.

slides.heading: *CL_SALV_TABLE*
slides.code:
cl_salv_table=>factory(
  IMPORTING r_salv_table = DATA(lo_alv)
  CHANGING  t_table      = lt_orders ).
lo_alv->get_functions( )->set_all( ).
lo_alv->display( ).
slides.voiceover: SALV table का factory call करो, अपनी table pass करो, toolbar on करो, और display.
slides.spoken: SALV table ka factory call karo, apni table pass karo, toolbar on karo, aur display.

slides.label: RECAP
slides.heading: *factory* then *display*
slides.body: Columns come from the table type automatically.
slides.voiceover: Columns अपने आप बन जाते हैं। Save कर लो।
slides.spoken: Columns apne aap ban jaate hain. Save kar lo.

posts.caption:
Still building a field catalog for every simple report?

CL_SALV_TABLE gives you a full ALV in a few lines:
1. factory( ) with your internal table
2. get_functions( )->set_all( ) for sort, filter and Excel export
3. display( )

Columns and headings come from the table type. Wrap the call in TRY...CATCH cx_salv_msg.

Which ALV do you use most: SALV or REUSE_ALV_GRID_DISPLAY?
